note: WRITTEN AND RED, 7 Sep, for a real defect. Instrument: acceptance.sh block AT20 plus test/at20-window-probe.mjs over CDP. It drives prez's OWN launch rather than a reconstruction: --browser points at a wrapper that appends a debugging port and execs the real browser, so prez builds and sends presenting_argv untouched and the probe measures the window that actually appeared. Rebuilding the argv in the harness would have been a second copy of exactly what AT15 deleted from chrome(). THREE LEGS. Cold default: PASS, 7 checks, window 1280x720 at aspect 1.78, the default read out of prez --help rather than written down here. Override: PASS, 7 checks, --window 900x600 gives 900x600 at 1.50 -- a different ASPECT on purpose, so a launch that ignored the flag fails on shape rather than sliding under a size tolerance. FORWARDED: FAIL. With an instance already running on the SAME profile, present --window 640x480 produced a 1024x768 window -- the size of the window already open. Page outerWidth and Browser.getWindowBounds agree, so it is the window and not the measurement. THE FINDING: AC19's geometry is COLD-START-ONLY. --window-size is honoured when Chrome cold-starts and ignored when the launch forwards into a running instance. This is the answer to utilz-cc's 29 Aug question, and it is very likely the explanation for the portrait window hv screenshotted that day -- which means AC19's remedy does not fix the case that PRODUCED AC19, since a user with Chrome already open is the normal case. AC19 cannot be marked satisfied as written: 'the presenting window opens at the deck's own shape' is false on the common path. hv's ruling needed. LIMITS: the forwarding behaviour is Chrome's, not prez's, and no flag combination tested here changes it; the probe proves the window Chrome opened for prez's argv and not what a window manager may do to it afterwards; and macOS only so far -- the Linux leg is unmeasured. || GREEN 7 Sep AGAINST THE REWORDED AC19 -- the wording moved, not the measurement, and the red above is kept because it is the finding. Cold default PASS (1280x720 at 1.78, the default read from prez --help). Override PASS (--window 900x600 -> 900x600 at 1.50). Forwarded PASS, now asserting INHERITANCE rather than the wish: with a 1024x768 window already open on the same profile, present --window 640x480 produced 1024x768. IT CAN STILL GO RED -- if a future Chrome honours --window-size on the forwarded path, the inheritance assertion fails and sends a reader back to the criterion, which is the right outcome rather than a silent improvement nobody notices. AC19(d)'s DOCUMENTATION clause is checked here too rather than merely claimed: help/prez.md must state the limit and say what to do about it, because a clause satisfied by someone remembering to write the page is not satisfied.
